title: Single-Cell Transcriptomic Profiling and Machine Learning Integration Unveil Stromal Cell Heterogeneity in Endometriosis.
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用单细胞转录组和机器学习分析子宫内膜异位症基质细胞异质性，但核心是疾病分型与生物标志物，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endometriosis (EMs) affects approximately 10% of reproductive-age women worldwide, yet its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Abnormal cell differentiation and somatic mutations in the ectopic endometrial microenvironment play critical roles in disease progression and treatment response heterogeneity. This study is aimed at elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying ectopic endometrial cell differentiation using machine learning (ML) approaches and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and identifying novel prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets, with particular attention to mutation-driven transcriptional alterations. METHODS: We analyzed comprehensive transcriptomic data from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and Human Endometrium Database (HED), including scRNA-seq data from 162,485 cells across 46 EMs patients. Through systematic comparative analysis, we identified 298 genes associated with ectopic endometrial cell differentiation, including genes harboring recurrent somatic mutations reported in endometriotic lesions. We evaluated 10 distinct ML algorithms and 101 hybrid combinations to develop predictive models for patient stratification. Unsupervised clustering analysis identified distinct patient phenotypes. Functional enrichment analysis, pathway analysis, and cell-cell communication networks were constructed to characterize the ectopic microenvironment. Four key genes (HOXA10, ESR1, MMP9, and SPP1) were validated by quantitative real-time PCR in normal endometrial stromal cells (NESCs) and ectopic endometrial stromal cells (EESCs). RESULTS: Unsupervised clustering revealed two distinct patient subgroups characterized as high- and low-invasive ectopic endometrium phenotypes with significantly different disease progression trajectories. Single-cell analysis unveiled extensive cellular heterogeneity within the ectopic endometrial microenvironment, identifying multiple cell types including epithelial, stromal, endothelial, and immune cells. Gene ontology and pathway enrichment analyses demonstrated significant activation of extracellular matrix organization, cell adhesion, cell migration, and angiogenesis pathways. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed macrophages as central mediators forming extensive connections with stromal, epithelial, and endothelial cells, with SPP1 emerging as a key signaling molecule. Trajectory analysis of stromal cells identified at least two major differentiation branches, indicating divergent differentiation programs. Notably, several of the 298 differentiation-associated genes overlapped with loci frequently mutated in ectopic lesions, suggesting that somatic mutations may contribute to aberrant gene regulation. qRT-PCR validation confirmed significant differential expression of key genes: HOXA10 showed 62% downregulation (0.38 +/- 0.06 vs. 1.00 +/- 0.09, p < 0.001), whereas ESR1, MMP9, and SPP1 demonstrated 108%, 252%, and 189% upregulation, respectively, in EESCs compared with NESCs (all p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: This study provides a comprehensive molecular characterization of ectopic endometrial cell differentiation through integrative ML-based analysis and single-cell sequencing. The identification of distinct patient phenotypes, key regulatory genes, and macrophage-centric communication networks advances our understanding of EMs pathogenesis. HOXA10, ESR1, MMP9, and SPP1 represent potential diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets for personalized treatment strategies. The convergence of mutation-associated transcriptional changes and differentiation abnormalities underscores the need for mutation-aware therapeutic strategies. These findings pave the way for developing more effective and targeted interventions to improve patient outcomes in EMs management.
abstract_zh: 背景：子宫内膜异位症（EMs）影响全球约10%的育龄女性，但其发病机制尚未完全阐明。异位子宫内膜微环境中的异常细胞分化和体细胞突变在疾病进展及治疗反应异质性中发挥关键作用。本研究旨在利用机器学习（machine learning, ML）方法和单细胞RNA测序（single-cell RNA sequencing, scRNA-seq）阐明异位子宫内膜细胞分化的分子机制，并识别新的预后生物标志物和治疗靶点，特别关注突变驱动的转录改变。方法：我们分析了来自基因表达综合数据库（Gene Expression Omnibus, GEO）和人类子宫内膜数据库（Human Endometrium Database, HED）的综合转录组数据，包括来自46例EMs患者的162,485个细胞的scRNA-seq数据。通过系统比较分析，我们鉴定了298个与异位子宫内膜细胞分化相关的基因，包括子宫内膜异位病灶中报道的携带反复体细胞突变的基因。我们评估了10种不同的ML算法和101种混合组合，以开发用于患者分层的预测模型。无监督聚类分析识别出不同的患者表型。构建了功能富集分析、通路分析和细胞-细胞通讯网络以表征异位微环境。四个关键基因（HOXA10、ESR1、MMP9和SPP1）通过定量实时PCR在正常子宫内膜基质细胞（NESCs）和异位子宫内膜基质细胞（EESCs）中得到验证。结果：无监督聚类揭示了两个不同的患者亚组，分别表现为高侵袭性和低侵袭性异位子宫内膜表型，其疾病进展轨迹显著不同。单细胞分析揭示了异位子宫内膜微环境内广泛的细胞异质性，识别出包括上皮细胞、基质细胞、内皮细胞和免疫细胞在内的多种细胞类型。基因本体和通路富集分析显示细胞外基质组织、细胞粘附、细胞迁移和血管生成通路显著激活。细胞-细胞通讯分析揭示巨噬细胞作为中心介质，与基质细胞、上皮细胞和内皮细胞形成广泛连接，其中SPP1作为关键信号分子出现。基质细胞的轨迹分析识别出至少两个主要分化分支，表明存在不同的分化程序。值得注意的是，298个分化相关基因中有多个与异位病灶中频繁突变的位点重叠，提示体细胞突变可能促成异常基因调控。qRT-PCR验证确认了关键基因的显著差异表达：与NESCs相比，EESCs中HOXA10显示62%的下调（0.38 ± 0.06 vs. 1.00 ± 0.09，p < 0.001），而ESR1、MMP9和SPP1分别显示108%、252%和189%的上调（均p < 0.001）。结论：本研究通过基于ML的整合分析和单细胞测序，提供了异位子宫内膜细胞分化的全面分子表征。不同患者表型、关键调控基因和以巨噬细胞为中心的通讯网络的识别，推进了我们对EMs发病机制的理解。HOXA10、ESR1、MMP9和SPP1代表了潜在诊断生物标志物和个性化治疗策略的治疗靶点。突变相关转录改变与分化异常的趋同强调了突变感知治疗策略的必要性。这些发现为开发更有效和靶向的干预措施以改善EMs管理中的患者结局铺平了道路。
